note: Ordered by how many people pass through, busiest first. Footfall is a published figure; the sessions an hour is a planning number the reader sets, seeded at 3 to 4 on Al's advice.

places.name: Broadway, the Honky Tonk Highway
places.visitors: most of Nashville's 16.9 million yearly visitors
places.note: The heart of the city's tourism. Free live music every day of the year, from morning until 3am.
places.footfall: the busiest street in the city

places.name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
places.note: One of the world's largest museums of American vernacular music.

places.name: Nashville Zoo at Grassmere
places.note: 188 acres, and the top paid attraction in Middle Tennessee.

places.name: Cheekwood Estate and Gardens
places.visitors: up to 435,000 in a peak year
places.note: 55 acres of botanical garden and art museum on a 1920s estate.

places.name: Grand Ole Opry House
places.visitors: over 250,000 a year on daytime tours alone
places.note: Home of the longest running live radio broadcast in US history, plus the evening show crowds.
places.footfall: over 250,000 a year on tours alone

places.name: Ryman Auditorium
places.note: The Mother Church of Country Music, in the building since 1892. More than 17 million people have been through it since it opened as a museum.

places.name: Gaylord Opryland Resort atrium
places.visitors: open to visitors who are not staying
places.note: Nine acres of indoor gardens, waterfalls and a river with flatboat rides.

places.name: John Seigenthaler Pedestrian Bridge
places.note: The clearest unobstructed view of the downtown skyline, and no traffic on it.
